{"id":"R06178","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Survey of agentic skills, not original empirical OS security research.","evidence":"A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills"},
{"id":"R06179","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM generates mobile app test scripts; no security outcome or OS security target.","evidence":"application of large language models (LLM) in the domain of mobile application test script generation"},
{"id":"R06180","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Drone command-and-control harness; security checks concern the agent interface, not OS components.","evidence":"gives any MCP-capable LLM command, telemetry, mission, and safety functions"},
{"id":"R06181","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM investigation of OS system provenance for intrusion detection and attack attribution.","evidence":"combines evidence curation with context-grounded LLM reasoning"},
{"id":"R06182","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM-assisted automated repair of TEE partitioning vulnerabilities with patch validation.","evidence":"automatically repairing bad partitioning issues in TEE applications"},
{"id":"R06183","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM agents perform evidence-grounded attack-chain reconstruction across multiple operating systems.","evidence":"attack chain reconstruction by retrieving and interpreting heterogeneous telemetry"},
{"id":"R06184","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Benchmark of behavioral jailbreaks against LLM agents; agent safety, not LLM use for OS security.","evidence":"behavior jailbreak, where an adversary induces an agent to execute dangerous OS-level operations"},
{"id":"R06185","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Local LLM deployment for translators; no security or OS security task.","evidence":"Local LLM Deployment for Translators"},
{"id":"R06186","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM incident-log analysis, but the target is not shown to be an OS component or privileged interface.","evidence":"segment-level ablation attribution to investigate incident logs of an actual cyberattack"},
{"id":"R06187","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Attacks and evaluates LLM coding agents via OS state composition; focus is agent security.","evidence":"exposing what we call CLI command-composition risk (CCR)"},
{"id":"R06188","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM generates security-policy DSL rules for Polkit, an OS authorization service.","evidence":"DSLs are widely used for managing operating system security policies"},
{"id":"R06189","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM code generation for GPU-accelerated cryptography; performance, not OS security analysis.","evidence":"GPU-friendly code generation using various LLMs"},
{"id":"R06190","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM translates adversary-emulation procedures across operating systems for structural security evaluation.","evidence":"Translating them across operating systems supports cross-platform defender evaluation"},
{"id":"R06191","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"General OS agent for user tasks; security is only listed as future work.","evidence":"evaluation paradigms, agent collaboration, and security"},
{"id":"R06192","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Characterizes command-denylist fragility in terminal AI agents; focus is agent security.","evidence":"first systematic characterization of command denylist fragility in terminal AI agents"},
{"id":"R06193","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Indirect prompt-injection benchmark for computer-use agents; security of LLM agents.","evidence":"low-harm injected goals"},
{"id":"R06194","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Position paper on LLMs as 6G RAN orchestrators; not OS security research.","evidence":"This position paper argues"},
{"id":"R06195","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Scientific-discovery agent workspace; operating system is used metaphorically with no security task.","evidence":"a unified, multi-modal operating system designed for Artificial Intelligence for Science"},
{"id":"R06196","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Forensic analysis of local LLM client artifacts, not LLM applied to OS security.","evidence":"systematic, cross platform forensic analysis of these popular local LLM clients"},
{"id":"R06197","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM/NLP mining of CTI reports; not targeted at OS components or privileged interfaces.","evidence":"mining temporal attack patterns from cyberthreat intelligence (CTI) reports"},
{"id":"R06198","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Position or overview on general-purpose AI risks; security of LLMs, not OS security application.","evidence":"Fundamental Risks in the Current Deployment of General-Purpose AI Models"},
{"id":"R06199","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM/RAG log analysis includes OS logs, but security-analysis focus and target specificity are ambiguous.","evidence":"produced by software applications, operating systems, servers, and network devices"},
{"id":"R06200","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Red-teaming computer-use agents to induce OS-level compromise; security of LLM agents.","evidence":"We target operating-system-level compromise"},
{"id":"R06201","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Audits scientific summary rigor; vulnerability is methodological, not OS security.","evidence":"post-retrieval auditing framework"},
{"id":"R06202","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Trust and verification schema for agent skill runtimes, not an OS security task.","evidence":"a skill is untrusted code until it is verified"},
{"id":"R06203","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM generates Unix CTF training tasks; no LLM security analysis or testing of OS components.","evidence":"LLM-assisted synthesis pipeline that generates candidate hiding techniques"},
{"id":"R06204","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM repair benchmark for eBPF verifier rejections in the Linux kernel.","evidence":"eBPF lets developers run custom programs inside the Linux kernel"},
{"id":"R06205","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Defense framework for securing AI agents on Kubernetes; LLM is the secured party.","evidence":"agent safety on Kubernetes is therefore an infrastructure problem"},
{"id":"R06206","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Kernel scheduler policy switching for LLM agents; OS performance work without a security outcome.","evidence":"switch scheduler behavior as the workload changes"},
{"id":"R06207","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM-guided network protocol fuzzing, but the abstract does not establish an OS network-stack target.","evidence":"A Dense Retrieval-based Multi-Agent System for Network Protocol Fuzzing"},
{"id":"R06208","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"Protocol fuzzing with LLM-assisted mutation; OS network-stack scope is not established.","evidence":"Greybox protocol fuzzing is a random testing approach for stateful protocol implementations"},
{"id":"R06209","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM-assisted fuzzing of network protocol implementations; OS component target is ambiguous.","evidence":"Testing network protocol implementations is critical"},
{"id":"R06210","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM fuzzing of industrial control protocols, not OS components or privileged interfaces.","evidence":"vulnerabilities in industrial control protocols (ICPs)"},
{"id":"R06211","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-assisted fuzzing of IoT HTTP services, not OS components.","evidence":"LLM-guided IoT HTTP fuzzing method"},
{"id":"R06212","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-assisted fuzzing of industrial control protocols, outside OS component scope.","evidence":"Industrial Control Protocols (ICPs)"},
{"id":"R06213","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM validation of network protocol parsers; whether these are OS network-stack components is unclear.","evidence":"Network protocol parsers are essential for enabling correct and secure communication between devices"},
{"id":"R06214","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM-driven security testing of cryptographic protocol implementations; OS target is not explicit.","evidence":"protocol security testing"},
{"id":"R06215","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-guided semantic fuzzing for general software targets; no OS component focus.","evidence":"LLM-Guided, Reasoning-Driven Input Mutation"},
{"id":"R06216","decision":"UNCLEAR","reason":"LLM extracts RFC rules to fuzz network protocol implementations; OS target is ambiguous.","evidence":"Semantics-Aware Fuzzing Framework for Network Protocol Implementations"},
{"id":"R06217","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-assisted fuzzing of cross-chain bridge contracts, not OS components.","evidence":"Cross-chain bridges move value between blockchains"}
]
